title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Nasdaq snapped a four-session losing streak (+0.4%) on a cybersecurity rally Wednesday, but the S&P 500 slid again (-0.2%) and the Dow fell 561pts (-1.1%); the 10-year Treasury yield eased to 5.07% on hawkish Fed talk.
Markets: Anthropic's IPO priced at $83/share (~$1.08T valuation); shares begin trading today (Nov. 19) on Nasdaq under ticker ANT, one of the largest tech listings on record.

Companies: Nvidia posted record sales and beat estimates, with interim CEO Colette Kress raising FY2028 revenue-growth guidance to 75% (from 70%) — but shares still slipped ~3% after Tuesday's report.

Companies: Cybersecurity stocks surged on outage-driven spending bets — Okta +12%, with Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike also among top gainers; Palo Alto beat earnings, raised its outlook, and is reportedly acquiring AI startup Applied Compute for $4-5B.

Companies: UnitedHealth and Humana tumbled by double-digit percentages, the S&P's biggest decliners, on concerns over expanded Medicare Advantage audits; Target's turnaround accelerated with +5.6% comp sales and raised profit guidance, credited to groceries and Pokémon merchandise.

Macro/Policy: Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a half-point rate hike in December may be warranted, citing inflation concerns — an unusually hawkish signal; a separate NY Fed official said a hike is likely within about three weeks.
Macro/Policy: Diesel prices dipped below $6/gallon for the first time in months even as wholesale food prices ran 1.7% above year-ago levels.
